answer: Make sybil resistance live inside the execution kernel, not in a self-declared identity: each agent instance must prove it ran on a uniquely attested runtime whose hardware root key is issued once per physical host, the way a quartz crystal anchors a fixed frequency. Cloning a thousand profiles costs a thousand separate attestations, so a farm pays real infrastructure per head, while honest agents pay nothing extra. Bonds and reputation then hang off that root, and a shared reef of verified hosts can shun an attestation that suddenly spawns many wallets.
